title: The Government's Position on the Presumptions under the Misuse of Drugs Act
what_it_is: The Government's Position on the Presumptions under the Misuse of Drugs Act

sections.label: Ministerial Statement on pending challenge
sections.summary: The Minister decided to make a Ministerial Statement because a case challenging the presumptions is pending before the Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But given the importance of the matter he has raised, I have decided to make a Ministerial Statement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There is a case pending before the Courts challenging the presumptions.

sections.label: No amendments to MDA presumptions
sections.summary: The Government has seen no reason to amend the presumptions, which date back to the MDA's enactment in 1973.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Government has seen no reason to introduce any amendments with regard to those presumptions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The MDA presumptions date back to the enactment of the MDA itself in 1973.

sections.label: Accused bears burden of proof
sections.summary: Under the MDA, the accused must prove he did not know the drugs found in his possession were drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Under the MDA, the onus is on the accused to prove that he did not know that what was found to be in his possession were drugs – and these are usually facts within his knowledge.

sections.label: Government to defend presumptions' constitutionality
sections.summary: The Government will defend the constitutionality of the presumptions, which may relate to a specific court challenge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Mr Zhulkarnain’s question may have arisen by reason of a specific challenge before the Courts, which I referred to earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I can say that the Government will defend the constitutionality of the presumptions.

sections.label: Reviewing MDA thresholds and assistance certificate
sections.summary: CNB and MHA review purity weights annually with HSA, and the Certificate of Substantive Assistance has been helpful overall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, 15 grammes of diamorphine or pure heroin, which would actually feed an addict for almost a year, or almost 200 abusers within one week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First question, would the Government be looking or how is the Government continually reviewing the fixed quantity thresholds of the MDA presumptions; possibly to take into account the actual patterns of drug abuse or trafficking, the changing drug markets and the new substances that are coming up?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this regard, is the Government studying the effectiveness of this discretionary sentencing on whether it is helping to apprehend more traffickers higher up on the supply chain, or an effective deterrence in this regard?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) and the Ministry of Home Affairs review the weight of the purities annually, and also in discussion with Health Sciences Authority (HSA), so that HSA can flag out if there are any anomalies, in terms of purities and weight that we need to look at.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the review is done annually, so that we make sure that it is proportionate and relevant to the patterns of consumption and the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the second question, on the whole, having the Certificate of Substantive Assistance has been helpful.
